title: Bubbling and capturing
learningObjectives: Explain bubbling and capturing and build modular, event-driven browser code.

understand.concept: Many user-interface events bubble from the target through ancestors. A listener registered with capture:true runs during the capture phase. Some events do not bubble, and event properties such as target and currentTarget refer to different elements during propagation.
understand.whyItMatters: Capturing and bubbling provide options for handling interactions at different levels of a DOM tree. They are also the foundation for event delegation.
understand.analogy: Capturing follows the path toward the clicked item; bubbling follows the path back toward the outer container.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; module loading and DOM event behaviour follow web platform standards.

explain.narrative: The capture listener runs before the target. The bubble listener runs later if the event bubbles; target is the origin and currentTarget is the element whose listener is executing.

examples.explanation: The capture listener runs before the target. The bubble listener runs later if the event bubbles; target is the origin and currentTarget is the element whose listener is executing.
examples.expectedOutput: Browser console output demonstrates module or event behaviour; DOM examples require matching elements.

practise.guidedTask: Compare event.target and event.currentTarget in a nested list. Test a non-bubbling event and explain the difference.
practise.independentTask: Build a small feature using explicit module boundaries or DOM event handling. Test keyboard, pointer, dynamic content, and failure cases as appropriate.
hints: Keep module responsibilities and public exports clear.
Preserve native keyboard and form behaviour.

questions.prompt: Which event property identifies the element whose listener is currently running?
questions.explanation: currentTarget is the element to which the current event listener is attached.

questions.prompt: What is a good principle for modular event-driven code?
options: Use clear contracts and preserve expected browser behaviour
Stop all propagation for every event
Expose every internal module binding globally
questions.answer: Use clear contracts and preserve expected browser behaviour
questions.explanation: Explicit interfaces and predictable event handling reduce coupling and preserve usability.
